subject.title: feat: add Podman agent sandbox backend

question: Should OpenClaw accept native Podman as a bundled local sandbox engine under the PR’s fail-closed remote-connection and browser-support constraints after a current-main rebase?
rationale: The implementation is a new security-relevant execution boundary; the existing maintainer comment resolves the core-versus-plugin placement but not the final acceptance of Podman’s operational and upgrade contract on the merge head.

options.title: Accept bundled Podman backend
options.body: Rebase, refresh focused proof, and merge with Podman kept as an opt-in built-in local-container backend under the documented connection restrictions.

options.title: Require a narrower boundary first
options.body: Keep the PR open while the owner narrows or changes the Podman runtime contract before deciding whether it can be supported in core.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Defer native Podman support if maintainers do not want to own a second local container-engine security boundary in this release window.

recommendation.title: Accept bundled Podman backend
recommendation.body: Rebase, refresh focused proof, and merge with Podman kept as an opt-in built-in local-container backend under the documented connection restrictions.

likelyOwner.reason: `sallyom` authored the current-head container refactor, is assigned to the PR, and posted the explicit maintainer recommendation about ownership placement.
